stories.title: 📜 Tobit 1
summaryBullets: The book of the words of Tobit son of Tobiel son of Hananiel son of Aduel son of Gabael son of Raphael son of Raguel of the descendants of Asiel, of the tribe of Naphtali, (1:1).

who in the days of King Shalmaneser of the Assyrians was taken into captivity from Thisbe, which is to the south of Kedesh Naphtali in Upper Galilee, above Asher toward the west, and north of Phogor. (1:2).

I, Tobit, walked in the ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life. I performed many acts of charity for my kindred and my nation who had gone with me in exile to Nineveh in the land of the Assyrians. (1:3).

When I was in my own country, in the land of Israel, while I was still a young man, the whole tribe of my ancestor Naphtali deserted the house of David and Jerusalem. This city had been chosen from among all the tribes of Israel, where all the tribes of Israel should offer sacrifice and where the temple, the dwelling of God, had been consecrated and established for all generations forever. (1:4).
All my kindred and my ancestral house of Naphtali sacrificed upon all the mountains of Galilee to the calf that King Jeroboam of Israel had erected in Dan and on all the mountains of Galilee. (1:5).

But I alone went often to Jerusalem for the festivals, as it is prescribed for all Israel by an everlasting decree. I would hurry off to Jerusalem with the first fruits of the crops and the firstlings of the flock, the tithes of the cattle, and the first shearings of the sheep. (1:6).

I would give these to the priests, the sons of Aaron, at the altar, likewise the tenth of the grain, wine, olive oil, pomegranates, figs, and the rest of the fruits to the sons of Levi who ministered at Jerusalem. Also every six years I would save up a second tenth in money and go and distribute it each year in Jerusalem, (1:7).

giving it to the orphans and widows and to the converts who had attached themselves to the Israelites. In the third year I would bring it and give it to them, and we would eat it according to the ordinance decreed concerning it in the law of Moses and according to the instructions of Deborah, the mother of my father Tobiel, for my father had died and left me an orphan. (1:8).
When I became a man I married a woman, a member of our own family, and by her I became the father of a son whom I named Tobias. (1:9).
After I was carried away captive to Assyria and came as a captive to Nineveh, everyone of my kindred and my people ate the food of the nations, (1:10).
but I kept myself from eating the food of the nations. (1:11).
Because I was mindful of God with all my heart, (1:12).
the Most High gave me favor and good standing with Shalmaneser, and I used to buy everything he needed. (1:13).
Until his death I used to go into Media to buy for him there, and I left in trust bags holding ten talents of silver with Gabael, the brother of Gabri, in the country of Media. (1:14).
But when Shalmaneser died and his son Sennacherib reigned in his place, Median roads became lawless, and I could no longer travel to Media. (1:15).
In the days of Shalmaneser I performed many acts of charity to my kindred, those of my people. (1:16).
I would give my food to the hungry and my clothing to the naked, and if I saw the dead body of any of my nation thrown out behind the wall of Nineveh, I would bury it. (1:17).

I also buried any whom King Sennacherib put to death when he came fleeing from Judea in those days of judgment that the King of heaven executed upon him because of his blasphemies. For in his anger he put to death many Israelites, but I would secretly remove the bodies and bury them. So when Sennacherib looked for them he could not find them. (1:18).

Then one of the Ninevites went and informed the king about me, that I was burying them, so I hid myself. But when I realized that the king knew about me and that I was being searched for to be put to death, I was afraid and ran away. (1:19).
Then all my property was confiscated; nothing was left to me that was not taken into the royal treasury except my wife Anna and my son Tobias. (1:20).

But not forty days passed before two of Sennacherib’s sons killed him, and when they fled to the mountains of Ararat, his son Esar-haddon reigned after him. He appointed Ahikar, the son of my brother Hanael, over all the accounts of his kingdom, and he had authority over the entire administration. (1:21).

Ahikar interceded for me, and I returned to Nineveh. Now Ahikar was chief cupbearer, keeper of the signet, and in charge of administration and accounts under King Sennacherib of Assyria, so Esar-haddon appointed him as second-in-command. He was my nephew and so a close relative. (1:22).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 17:5-6: Shalmaneser takes Samaria and deports Israel to Assyria and the cities of the Medes.
1 Kings 12:28-30: Jeroboam sets up the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
Deuteronomy 14:22-29: The tithes, including the third-year tithe for Levites, aliens, orphans, and widows.
2 Kings 19:35-37: Sennacherib returns from Judah, is killed by two of his sons, and Esar-haddon reigns in his place.
Deuteronomy 16:16: Every male appears before the LORD three times a year at the place He chooses.

translationNotes.note: A unit of weight and of money, not a skill or ability. One talent equals 3,000 shekels, roughly 30 kilograms or 66 pounds of silver. The ten talents Tobit leaves with Gabael are about 300 kilograms of metal, a fortune that has to be carried by pack animal.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἄρτοι τῶν ἐθνῶν (artoi ton ethnon)
translationNotes.note: Literally the bread of the Gentiles: food bought, slaughtered, or prepared without regard to the dietary rules of Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14. Refusing it was the visible marker of a Jew living inside a foreign administration.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי (maaser sheni) - Greek: δεκάτη (dekate)
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 14:22-27 lets a worshiper who lives too far from the sanctuary sell the tithe, carry the silver to Jerusalem, and spend it there; 14:28-29 assigns a third-year tithe to the poor. Tobit describes doing both.

The signet was a ring or cylinder that stamped the king's mark into clay or wax. Whoever held it could seal documents in the king's name, so Ahikar's titles of cupbearer, signet keeper, and chief of accounts describe the top of the royal administration.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobit of Naphtali, captive in Nineveh, alone kept the Jerusalem festivals while his tribe sacrificed to Jeroboam's calf. He refuses Gentile food, leaves ten talents of silver with Gabael in Media, and buries Israelites Sennacherib kills. Denounced, he flees and loses all, then Ahikar intercedes.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 2
summaryBullets: In the days of Esar-haddon I returned home, and my wife Anna and my son Tobias were restored to me. At our Festival of Pentecost, which is the sacred Festival of Weeks, a good dinner was prepared for me, and I reclined to eat. (2:1).

When the table had been set for me and an abundance of food placed before me, I said to my son Tobias, “Go, my son, and bring whatever poor person you may find of our kindred among the exiles in Nineveh who is wholeheartedly mindful of God, and he shall eat together with me. I will wait for you, my son, until you come back.” (2:2).

So Tobias went to look for some poor person of our kindred. When he had returned he said, “Father!” And I replied, “Here I am, my son.” Then he went on to say, “Look, father, one of our own nation has been killed and thrown into the marketplace, and now he lies there strangled.” (2:3).
Then I sprang up, left the dinner before even tasting it, and removed him from the square and laid him in one of the outbuildings at my home until sunset, when I might bury him. (2:4).
When I returned, I washed myself and ate my food in sorrow. (2:5).
Then I remembered the prophecy of Amos, how he said against Bethel, “Your festivals shall be turned into mourning and all your songs into lamentation.” And I wept. (2:6).
When the sun had set, I went and dug a grave and buried him. (2:7).
And my neighbors laughed and said, “Is he still not afraid? He has already been hunted down to be put to death for doing this, and he ran away, yet here he is again burying the dead!” (2:8).
That same night I washed myself and went into my courtyard and lay down by the wall of the courtyard; my face was uncovered because of the heat. (2:9).

I did not know that there were sparrows on the wall; their fresh droppings fell into my eyes and produced white films. I went to physicians to be healed, but the more they treated me with ointments, the more my vision was obscured by the white films, until I became completely blind. For four years I remained unable to see. All my kindred were sorry for me, and Ahikar took care of me for two years before he went to Elymais. (2:10).
At that time my wife Anna earned money at women’s work. (2:11).

She used to send what she made to the owners, and they would pay wages to her. One day, the seventh of Dystrus, when she cut off a piece she had woven and sent it to the owners, they paid her full wages and also gave her a young goat for a meal. (2:12).

When it came toward me, the goat began to bleat, so I called her and said, “Where did you get this goat? It is surely not stolen, is it? Return it to the owners, for we have no right to eat anything stolen.” (2:13).

But she said to me, “It was given to me as a gift in addition to my wages.” But I did not believe her and told her to return it to the owners. I became flushed with anger against her over this. Then she replied to me, “Where are your acts of charity? Where are your righteous deeds? These things are known about you!” (2:14).
crossRefs: Leviticus 23:15-21: The Festival of Weeks, kept fifty days after the sheaf offering.
Amos 8:10: Festivals turned into mourning and songs into lamentation, the words Tobit remembers.
Deuteronomy 21:22-23: A body must be buried the same day and not left exposed overnight.
Numbers 19:11-13: Touching a corpse makes a person unclean and requires washing.
Job 2:9-10: An afflicted man answered bitterly by his wife.

translationNotes.note: The wheat-harvest feast of Leviticus 23:15-21, counted fifty days from the sheaf offering. Pentekoste is simply Greek for fiftieth, so both names in the verse mark one and the same day.

Deuteronomy 21:22-23 requires same-day burial, and leaving a corpse exposed was treated across the ancient Near East as the ultimate disgrace and a deterrent used against the executed. Tobit recovers bodies the authorities meant to leave lying, which is why the work is done at sunset and why he is hunted for it.
A medical term for whitish opacity spreading over the surface of the eye. Ancient physicians treated it with salves and ointments, which is exactly what the text says failed for Tobit.
Dystros is a month of the Macedonian calendar, used widely across the kingdoms of the east, falling roughly in February and March. The Greek text dates Anna's payday by it.

stories.keyTakeaway: At the Festival of Weeks Tobit leaves his dinner untasted to bury an Israelite murdered in the marketplace, and neighbors mock him. That night sparrow droppings fall into his eyes and leave white films that blind him four years. Anna is given a goat with her wages, and he calls it stolen.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 3
summaryBullets: Then with much grief and anguish of heart I wept, and with groaning I began to pray: (3:1).
“You are righteous, O Lord, and all your deeds are just; all your ways are mercy and truth; you judge the world. (3:2).
And now, O Lord, may you be mindful of me and look favorably upon me. Do not punish me for my sins or for my unwitting offenses or for those of my ancestors. They sinned against you (3:3).

and disobeyed your commandments. So you gave us over to plunder, exile, and death, to become the talk, the byword, and an object of reproach among all the nations among whom you have dispersed us. (3:4).
And now your many judgments are true in dealing with me according to my sins. For we have not kept your commandments and have not walked in accordance with truth before you. (3:5).

So now deal with me as you will; command my spirit to be taken from me, so that I may be released from the face of the earth and become dust. For it is better for me to die than to live, because I have had to listen to undeserved insults, and great is the sorrow that attends me. Command, O Lord, that I be released from this distress; release me to go to the place of eternity, and do not, O Lord, turn your face away from me. For it is better for me to die than to see so much distress in my life and better not to listen to insults.” (3:6).
On the same day, at Ecbatana in Media, it also happened that Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, was reproached by one of her father’s female slaves. (3:7).

For she had been married to seven husbands, and the wicked demon Asmodeus had killed each of them before they had been with her as is customary for wives. So the female slave said to her, “You are the one who kills your husbands! See, you have already been married to seven husbands and have not borne the name of a single one of them. (3:8).
Why do you beat us? Because your husbands are dead? Go with them! May we never see a son or daughter of yours!” (3:9).

Overcome with emotion at that time, she wept and went up to her father’s upper room, intending to hang herself. But she thought it over and said, “Let no one ever reproach my father, saying to him, ‘You had only one beloved daughter, and she hanged herself out of distress!’ I would bring my father in his old age down in sorrow to Hades. It is better for me not to hang myself but to beg the Lord that I may die, so that I will not have to listen to these reproaches for the rest of my life.” (3:10).
At that same time, with hands outstretched toward the window, she prayed and said, “Blessed are you, merciful God! Blessed is your name forever; let all your works bless you forever. (3:11).
And now, my face is toward you, and I have raised my eyes. (3:12).
Command that I be released from the earth and not listen to such reproaches any more. (3:13).
You know, O Master, that I am innocent of any defilement with a man (3:14).

and that I have not disgraced my name or the name of my father in the land of my exile. I am my father’s only child; he has no other child to be his heir, and he has no close relative or other kindred for whom I should keep myself as wife. Already seven husbands of mine have died. Why should I still live? But if it is not pleasing to you, O Lord, to take my life, hear me in my disgrace.” (3:15).
At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard in the glorious presence of God. (3:16).

So Raphael was sent to heal both of them: Tobit by removing the white films from his eyes, so that he might see God’s light with his eyes, and Sarah, daughter of Raguel, by giving her in marriage to Tobias son of Tobit, and by setting her free from the wicked demon Asmodeus. For Tobias was entitled to have her before all others who had desired to marry her. At the same time that Tobit returned from the courtyard into his house, Sarah daughter of Raguel came down from her upper room. (3:17).
crossRefs: Job 7:15-16: A suffering man who chooses death and loathes his life.
1 Kings 19:4: Elijah asks the LORD to take his life.
Genesis 38:6-11: Successive husbands of one woman die, and the surviving kin fear giving her another.
Psalm 34:15-18: The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous and His ears open to their cry.
Daniel 9:20-23: An answer sent out while the prayer is still being spoken.

translationNotes.note: The name the Greek text gives the demon who kills Sarah's husbands; later Jewish writings call him Ashmedai. He is an evil spirit acting against people, not a god and not a ghost of the dead.

The capital of Media, on the plain below Mount Alvand at modern Hamadan in western Iran. It lies roughly 400 miles (600 km) east of Nineveh, so the two scenes of this chapter happen a long caravan journey apart.

The Greek word standing in for Hebrew Sheol, the realm of the dead. To bring a parent down to Hades in sorrow is an idiom for sending him to the grave in grief, the same expression Jacob uses in Genesis 42:38.

A roof chamber built above the main house and often reached by an outside stair. It was the private space of the household, used for guests, illness, and prayer, which is why Sarah goes up there alone and prays at its window.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobit prays that God take his life. The same day at Ecbatana, Sarah is taunted because Asmodeus killed seven husbands, and she prays to die too. Both prayers are heard, and Raphael is sent to heal them: to take the white films from Tobit's eyes and free Sarah from the demon for Tobias.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 4
summaryBullets: That same day Tobit remembered the money that he had left in trust with Gabael at Rages in Media, (4:1).
and he said to himself, “Now that I have asked for death, why do I not call my son Tobias and explain to him about this money before I die?” (4:2).

Then he called his son Tobias, and when he came to him he said, “Give me a proper burial. Honor your mother and do not abandon her all the days of her life. Do whatever pleases her, and do nothing that makes her unhappy. (4:3).
Remember her, my son, because she faced many dangers for you while you were in her womb. And when she dies, bury her beside me in the same grave. (4:4).
“Be mindful of the Lord all your days, my son, and refuse to sin or to transgress his commandments. Do what is right all the days of your life, and do not walk in the ways of wrongdoing, (4:5).
for those who act honestly will prosper in all their activities. To all those who practice righteousness, (4:6).
give alms according to your circumstances, my son, and do not turn your face away from anyone who is poor. Then the face of God will not be turned away from you. (4:7).
Act according to what you have, my son. If you have much, give alms from it; if you have little, give alms in accordance with what you have. Do not be afraid, my son, to give alms. (4:8).
You will be laying up a good treasure for yourself against a day of need. (4:9).
For almsgiving delivers from death and keeps you from going into the darkness. (4:10).
Indeed, almsgiving, for all who practice it, is an excellent offering in the presence of the Most High. (4:11).

“Beware, my son, of every kind of sexual immorality. First of all, marry a woman from among the descendants of your ancestors; do not marry a foreign woman, who is not of your father’s tribe, for we are the descendants of prophets and true-born sons of prophets. The first prophet was Abraham, then Isaac and Jacob, our ancestors of old. Remember, my son, that these all took wives from among their kindred. They were blessed in their children, and their posterity will inherit the land. (4:12).

So now, my son, love your kindred, and in your heart do not be so arrogant against the daughters of the members of your people as to refuse to take one of them as a wife. For in arrogance there is ruin and great confusion, and in idleness there is loss and dire poverty, because idleness is the mother of famine. (4:13).

“Do not keep over until the next day the wages of those who work for you, but pay them their wages the same day, and let not the pay of those among you be delayed overnight. Your pay will not be kept over if you serve God faithfully. Watch yourself, my son, in everything you do, and discipline yourself in all your conduct. (4:14).
And what you hate, do not do to anyone. May no evil go with you on any of your way. (4:15).
Give some of your food to the hungry and some of your clothing to the naked. Give all your surplus as alms, my son, and do not let your eye begrudge your giving of alms. (4:16).
Pour out your food and your wine on the grave of the righteous, but do not give it to sinners. (4:17).
Seek advice from every wise person, and do not be disdainful, since any counsel is useful. (4:18).

At all times bless God and ask him that your ways may be made straight and that all your paths and plans may prosper. For no nation has good counsel, but the Lord himself gives it. Whom he wants to, he exalts, and whom he wants to, he casts down to Hades below. So now, my son, remember these commandments of mine, and do not let them be erased from your heart. (4:19).
“And now, my son, let me explain to you that I left ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael son of Gabrias, at Rages in Media. (4:20).
Do not be afraid, my son, because we have become poor. You have great wealth if you fear God and flee from every sin and do what is good in the sight of the Lord your God.” (4:21).
crossRefs: Exodus 20:12: Honor your father and your mother.
Deuteronomy 24:14-15: Pay a hired worker his wages the same day, before sunset.
Genesis 24:3-4: Abraham sends for a wife from his own kindred rather than the Canaanites.
Proverbs 19:17: Whoever is generous to the poor lends to the LORD.
Matthew 7:12: Do to others what you would have them do to you, the positive form of Tobit's rule.

translationNotes.note: Gifts of food, clothing, or money to the poor. The Hebrew word behind the Greek means righteousness, so in this book giving to the needy and doing right are named by the same word. English alms is a worn-down form of eleemosyne.

A deposit placed with a trusted person for safekeeping and reclaimed later. Long roads and bandits made carrying silver dangerous, so a traveler left the metal with a reliable host in a distant city and kept a written token to claim it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִשְׁפָּחָה (mishpachah) - Greek: σπέρμα τῶν πατέρων (sperma ton pateron)
translationNotes.note: Marriage inside the extended family or tribe. Exiled Israelite families used it to keep land, inheritance, and lineage intact, which is also why brother and sister in this book usually mean relative rather than sibling.

translationNotes.term: Food and wine on the grave
translationNotes.note: Setting out bread and wine at a tomb was a widespread funeral custom in the ancient world, an offering made on behalf of the dead. The instruction here restricts the practice to the graves of the righteous.

stories.keyTakeaway: Believing he is about to die, Tobit charges Tobias to bury his parents, keep the commandments, give alms from what he has, marry a woman of his own kindred, pay a worker the same day, and do to no one what he hates. Then he names the ten talents of silver left in trust with Gabael at Rages.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 5
summaryBullets: Then Tobias answered his father Tobit, “I will do everything that you have commanded me, father, (5:1).

but how can I obtain the money from him, since he does not know me and I do not know him? What evidence am I to give him so that he will recognize and trust me and give me the money? Also, I do not know the roads to Media or how to get there.” (5:2).

Then Tobit answered his son Tobias, “He gave me his bond, and I gave him my bond. I divided his in two; we each took one part, and I put one with the money. And now twenty years have passed since I left this money in trust. So now, my son, find yourself a trustworthy man to go with you, and we will pay him wages until you return. But get back the money from Gabael.” (5:3).

So Tobias went out to look for a man to go with him to Media, someone who was acquainted with the way. He went out and found the angel Raphael standing in front of him, but he did not perceive that he was an angel of God. (5:4).

Tobias said to him, “Where do you come from, young man?” “From the Israelites, your kindred,” he replied, “and I have come here to work.” Then Tobias said to him, “Do you know the way to go to Media?” (5:5).

“Yes,” he replied, “I have been there many times; I am acquainted with it and know all the roads. I have often traveled to Media and would stay with our kinsman Gabael who lives in Rages of Media. It is a journey of two days from Ecbatana to Rages, for it lies in a mountainous area, while Ecbatana is in the middle of the plain.” (5:6).
Then Tobias said to him, “Wait for me, young man, until I go in and tell my father, for I do need you to travel with me, and I will pay you your wages.” (5:7).
He replied, “All right, I will wait, but do not take too long.” (5:8).

So Tobias went in to tell his father Tobit and said to him, “I have just found a man who is one of our own Israelite kindred!” He replied, “Call the man in so that I may learn about his people and to what tribe he belongs and whether he is trustworthy enough to go with you, my son.” (5:9).

Then Tobias went out and called him and said, “Young man, my father is calling for you.” So he went in to him, and Tobit greeted him first. He replied, “Many greetings to you!” But Tobit retorted, “What is left for me to greet any more? I am a man without eyesight; I cannot see the light of heaven, but I lie in darkness like the dead who no longer see the light. Although still alive, I am among the dead. I hear people’s voices, but I cannot see them.” But the young man said, “Take courage; the time is near for God to heal you; take courage.” Then Tobit said to him, “My son Tobias wishes to go to Media. Can you accompany him and guide him? I will pay your wages, brother.” He answered, “I can go with him, and I know all the roads. I have often gone to Media, have crossed all its plains, and am familiar with its mountains and all of its roads.” (5:10).
Then Tobit said to him, “Brother, of what family are you and from what tribe? Tell me, brother.” (5:11).

He replied, “Why do you need to know my tribe and lineage? Are you seeking an employee or a tribe and lineage?” But Tobit said, “I want to be sure, brother, whose son you are and what your name is.” (5:12).
He replied, “I am Azariah, the son of the elder Hananiah, one of your relatives.” (5:13).

Then Tobit said to him, “You are very welcome, brother. Do not feel bitter toward me, brother, because I wanted to be sure about your family. It turns out that you are a kinsman and of good and noble lineage. For I knew Hananiah and Nathan, the two sons of the elder Shemeliah, and they used to go with me to Jerusalem and worship with me there; they were not led astray. Your kindred are good people; you are of good stock. Welcome!” (5:14).
Then he added, “I will pay you a drachma a day as wages, as well as expenses for yourself and my son. So go with my son, (5:15).
and I will add something to your wages.” Raphael answered, “I will go with him, so do not fear. We shall leave in good health and return to you in good health because the way is safe.” (5:16).

So Tobit said to him, “Blessings be upon you, brother.” Then he called his son and said to him, “Make preparations for the journey, my son, and set out with your brother. May God in heaven bring you safely there and return you in good health to me, and may his angel, my son, accompany you both for your safety.” Before he went out to start his journey, he kissed his father and mother. Tobit then said to him, “Have a safe journey.” (5:17).
But his mother began to weep and said to Tobit, “Why is it that you have sent my son away? Is he not the staff of our hand as he goes in and out before us? (5:18).
Do not heap money upon money, but let it be a ransom for our son. (5:19).
The life that is given to us by the Lord is enough for us.” (5:20).

Tobit said to her, “Do not worry; our son will leave in good health and return to us in good health. Your eyes will see him on the day when he returns to you in good health. Say no more! Do not fear for them, my sister, (5:21).
for a good angel will accompany him; his journey will be successful, and he will come back in good health.” (5:22).
crossRefs: Genesis 38:17-18: A pledge handed over as a token, to be produced later as proof of identity.
2 Kings 17:6: Israelites deported to Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes, where Gabael lives.
Genesis 42:38: A father fears the road will take his son and bring his own gray head down in sorrow.
Leviticus 19:13: The wages of a hired worker are not to be kept back overnight.
Psalm 91:11: He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.

translationNotes.note: A handwritten note recording a debt or a deposit. Tobit divided the document so each man held half; matching the two halves proved the bearer's claim. Greeks called such a matched token a symbolon, a broken piece that fits only its own other half.

A Greek silver coin of about 4.3 grams, the standard pay for one day of ordinary labor. Tobit offers a day's wage for each day of the journey plus the travelers' expenses, the same rate as the denarius a day in Matthew 20:2.

The highland country east of Assyria, in what is now western Iran. Its chief city Ecbatana sits at modern Hamadan, and Rages lies about 180 miles (290 km) further northeast at modern Rey, on the southern edge of Tehran. Assyria settled deported Israelites in these towns.

In this book brother and sister regularly mean kinsman or fellow Israelite rather than sibling. Tobit greets a stranger as brother, calls his own wife sister, and the marriage language later in the story uses the same words.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobit shows Tobias the bond he tore in two as proof for Gabael and sends him to hire a guide. He finds the angel Raphael without knowing it; Raphael gives his name as Azariah son of the elder Hananiah and is hired at a drachma a day. Anna weeps, and Tobit says a good angel will go with them.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 6
summaryBullets: So she stopped weeping. The young man went out, and the angel went with him, (6:1).
and the dog came out with him and went along with them. So they both journeyed along, and when the first night overtook them they camped by the Tigris River. (6:2).
Then the young man went down to wash his feet in the Tigris River, and a large fish leaped up from the water and tried to swallow the young man’s foot, and he cried out. (6:3).
But the angel said to the young man, “Catch hold of the fish and hang on to it!” So the young man grasped the fish and drew it up on the land. (6:4).

Then the angel said to him, “Cut open the fish and take out its gall, heart, and liver. Keep them with you, but throw away the intestines. For its gall, heart, and liver are useful as medicine.” (6:5).

So after cutting open the fish the young man gathered together the gall, heart, and liver; then he roasted and ate some of the fish and kept some to be salted for the journey. The two continued on their way together until they were near Media. (6:6).
Then the young man questioned the angel and said to him, “Azariah, my brother, what medicinal value is there in the fish’s heart and liver and in the gall?” (6:7).

He replied, “As for the fish’s heart and liver, you must burn them to make a smoke in the presence of a man or woman afflicted by a demon or evil spirit, and every affliction will flee away and never remain with that person any longer. (6:8).
And as for the gall, anoint a person’s eyes where white films have appeared on them; blow upon them, upon the white films, and the eyes will be healed.” (6:9).
When they entered Media and were already approaching Ecbatana, (6:10).

Raphael said to the young man, “Tobias, my brother.” “Here I am,” he answered. Then Raphael said to him, “We must stay this night in the home of Raguel. That man is your relative, and he has a daughter named Sarah. (6:11).

He has no male heir and no daughter except Sarah only, and you, as next of kin to her, have before all other men a hereditary claim on her. Also, it is right for you to inherit her father’s possessions. Moreover, the young woman is intelligent, brave, and very beautiful, and her father is a good man.” (6:12).

He continued, “You have every right to take her in marriage. So listen to me, brother; tonight I will speak to her father about the young woman, so that we may take her to be your bride. When we return from Rages we will celebrate her marriage. For I know that Raguel can by no means keep her from you or promise her to another man without incurring the penalty of death according to the decree of the book of Moses. Indeed, he knows that you, rather than any other man, are entitled to marry his daughter. So now listen to me, brother, and tonight we shall speak concerning the young woman and arrange her engagement to you. And when we return from Rages, we will take her and bring her back with us to your house.” (6:13).

Then Tobias said in answer to Raphael, “Azariah, my brother, I have heard that she already has been married to seven husbands and that they died in the bridal chamber. On the night when they went in to her, they would die. And I have heard some say that a demon kills them. (6:14).

It does not harm her, but it kills anyone who desires to approach her. So now, since I am the only son my father has, I am afraid that I may die and bring my father’s and mother’s lives down to their graves, grieving for me—and they have no other son to bury them.” (6:15).

But Raphael said to him, “Do you not remember your father’s orders when he commanded you to take a wife from your father’s house? Now listen to me, brother, and say no more about this demon. Take her. I know that this very night she will be given to you in marriage. (6:16).
When you enter the bridal chamber, take some of the fish’s liver and heart and put them on the embers of the incense. An odor will be given off; (6:17).

the demon will smell it and flee and will never be seen near her any more. Now when you are about to go to bed with her, both of you must first stand up and pray, imploring the Lord of heaven that mercy and safety may be granted to you. Do not be afraid, for she has always been set apart for you. You will save her, and she will go with you. I know that you will have children by her, and they will be as brothers and sisters to you. Now say no more!” When Tobias heard the words of Raphael and learned that she was his sister, related through his father’s lineage, he loved her very much, and his heart was drawn to her. (6:18).
crossRefs: Numbers 36:6-9: A daughter who inherits must marry within her father's clan so the inheritance stays in the family.
Numbers 27:8-11: The order of inheritance when a man leaves no son, giving the nearest kin the claim.
Deuteronomy 25:5-10: The duty of the nearest kinsman to marry into the family and preserve a man's name.
Genesis 24:12-27: A traveler on a marriage errand is led to the right kinswoman at journey's end.
Leviticus 16:12-13: Incense laid on burning coals so that the smoke rises.

translationNotes.note: The bitter fluid stored in the gall bladder. Greek and Roman medical writers list fish gall among the ingredients of eye salves used against films on the cornea, so the instruction here is a physician's remedy applied to a physical complaint.

Pharmakon means a drug or remedy of any kind. The organs are dried and laid on the live coals of an incense burner to raise a strong smoke, a standard ancient method of treating a room and the people in it.

The law of Moses kept land and family line inside the clan. A daughter who inherits marries within her father's tribe (Numbers 36:6-9), and the nearest kinsman is obliged to marry into the family to preserve a name (Deuteronomy 25:5-10). That is the decree of the book of Moses named here, and it is why Tobias ranks ahead of every other suitor.
The river that runs past Nineveh, named in Genesis 2:14 as one of the four rivers of Eden. The travelers' first night out of the city is spent on its bank.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobias travels with the angel and his dog. At the Tigris a large fish attacks him; he hauls it ashore and keeps the gall, heart, and liver as medicine. Nearing Ecbatana, Raphael tells him Sarah is his by kinship, and when he fears the demon that killed her husbands, tells him how to use the fish.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 7
summaryBullets: Now when they entered Ecbatana, Tobias said to him, “Azariah, my brother, take me straight to our brother Raguel.” So he took him to Raguel’s house, where they found him sitting beside the courtyard door. They greeted him first, and he replied, “Many greetings, my brothers; welcome and good health!” Then he brought them into his house. (7:1).
He said to his wife Edna, “How much this young man resembles my kinsman Tobit!” (7:2).
Then Edna questioned them, saying, “Where are you from, my brothers?” They answered her, “We belong to the descendants of Naphtali who are exiles in Nineveh.” (7:3).
She said to them, “Do you know our kinsman Tobit?” And they replied, “Yes, we know him.” Then she asked them, “Is he in good health?” (7:4).
They replied, “He is alive and in good health.” And Tobias added, “He is my father!” (7:5).
At that Raguel jumped up and kissed him and wept. (7:6).

He also spoke to him as follows, “Blessings on you, my son, offspring of a good and noble father! O most miserable of calamities that such an upright and beneficent man has become blind!” He then embraced his kinsman Tobias and wept. (7:7).
His wife Edna also wept for him, and their daughter Sarah likewise wept. (7:8).

Then Raguel slaughtered a ram from the flock and received them very warmly. When they had bathed and washed themselves and had reclined to dine, Tobias said to Raphael, “Azariah, my brother, ask Raguel to give me my sister Sarah.” (7:9).

But Raguel overheard it and said to the young man, “Eat and drink, and be merry tonight. For no one except you, brother, has the right to marry my daughter Sarah. Likewise I am not at liberty to give her to any other man than you because you are my nearest relative. But let me explain to you the true situation more fully, my son. (7:10).

I have given her to seven men of our kinsmen, and all died on the night when they went in to her. But now, my son, eat and drink, and the Lord will act on behalf of you both.” But Tobias said, “I will neither eat nor drink anything until you settle the things that pertain to me.” So Raguel said, “I will do so. She is given to you in accordance with the decree in the book of Moses, and it has been decreed from heaven that she be given to you. Take your sister; from now on you are her brother, and she is your sister. She is given to you from today and forever. May the Lord of heaven, my son, guide and prosper you both this night and grant you mercy and peace.” (7:11).

Then Raguel summoned his daughter Sarah. When she came to him, he took her by the hand and gave her to Tobias, saying, “Take her to be your wife in accordance with the law and decree written in the book of Moses. Take her and bring her safely to your father. And may the God of heaven let your journey go smoothly and in his peace.” (7:12).

Then he called her mother and told her to bring writing material, and he wrote out a copy of a marriage contract, to the effect that he gave her to him as wife according to the decree of the law of Moses. (7:13).
Then they began to eat and drink. (7:14).
Raguel called his wife Edna and said to her, “Sister, get the other room ready, and take her there.” (7:15).

So she went and made the bed in the room as he had told her and brought Sarah there. She wept for her daughter. Then, wiping away the tears, she said to her, “Take courage, my daughter; the Lord of heaven grant you joy in place of your sorrow. Take courage, my daughter.” Then she went out. (7:16).
crossRefs: Genesis 29:13-14: Laban embraces a kinsman who arrives from far off and calls him his own flesh and bone.
Genesis 24:33: A guest refuses to eat until his errand has been stated and settled.
Genesis 24:50-51: The bride's family answers that the matter comes from the LORD and gives her.
Deuteronomy 25:5-10: The marriage duty of the nearest kinsman that Raguel invokes as written law.
Genesis 18:6-7: A host runs to the herd and prepares an animal for arriving guests.

translationNotes.note: A written document recording the terms on which a father gave his daughter and the obligations the husband took on. The same practice appears in Jewish marriage contracts written on papyrus in the fifth century BC at the Jewish colony of Elephantine in Egypt.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֵפֶר מֹשֶׁה (sefer Mosheh) - Greek: βιβλίον Μωυσέως (biblion Mouseos)
translationNotes.note: The five books of the law, cited here as a written and binding text. Raguel treats its marriage rules as enforceable in Media, hundreds of miles outside the land of Israel.
Meat was rare in an everyday meal. Killing an animal from the flock for arriving guests was the highest form of welcome, the same gesture Abraham makes for his visitors at Mamre.

A standard Greek word of encouragement, roughly be brave or take heart, used to steady someone in fear or grief. It recurs through this book and is the same word Jesus speaks to the paralytic in Matthew 9:2.

stories.keyTakeaway: At Ecbatana Raguel and Edna welcome the travelers and weep to learn Tobias is Tobit's son. Tobias has Raphael ask for Sarah; Raguel says plainly that seven husbands have died and no other man has the right to her, gives her by the book of Moses, and writes a marriage contract.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 8
summaryBullets: When they had finished eating and drinking, they wanted to retire, so they took the young man and brought him into the bedroom. (8:1).
Then Tobias remembered the words of Raphael, and he took the fish’s liver and heart out of the bag where he had them and put them on the embers of the incense. (8:2).
The odor of the fish so repelled the demon that he fled to the remotest parts of Egypt. But Raphael followed him and at once bound him there hand and foot. (8:3).
When the parents had gone out and shut the door of the room, Tobias got out of bed and said to Sarah, “Sister, get up, and let us pray and implore our Lord that he grant us mercy and safety.” (8:4).

So she got up, and they began to pray and implore that they might be kept safe. Tobias began by saying, “Blessed are you, O God of our ancestors, and blessed is your name in all generations forever. Let the heavens and the whole creation bless you forever. (8:5).

You made Adam, and for him you made his wife Eve as a helper and support. From the two of them the human race has sprung. You said, ‘It is not good that the man should be alone; let us make a helper for him like himself.’ (8:6).
I now am taking this sister of mine, not for sexual gratification, but with sincerity. Grant that she and I may find mercy and that we may grow old together.” (8:7).
And they both together said, “Amen, Amen.” (8:8).
Then they went to sleep for the night. But Raguel arose and called his servants to him, and they went and dug a grave, (8:9).
for he said, “It is possible that he will die, and we will become an object of ridicule and derision.” (8:10).
When they had finished digging the grave, Raguel went into his house and called his wife, (8:11).
saying, “Send one of the female slaves and have her go in to see if he is alive. But if he is dead, let us bury him without anyone knowing it.” (8:12).
So they sent the female slave, lit a lamp, and opened the door; and she went in and found them lying in bed asleep together. (8:13).
Then the female slave came out and informed them that he was alive and that nothing was wrong. (8:14).
So they blessed the God of heaven, and Raguel said, “Blessed are you, O God, with every pure blessing; let all your chosen ones bless you. Let them bless you forever. (8:15).
Blessed are you because you have made me glad. It has not turned out as I expected, but you have dealt with us according to your great mercy. (8:16).
Blessed are you because you had compassion on two only children. Be merciful to them, O Master, and keep them safe; bring their lives to fulfillment in happiness and mercy.” (8:17).
Then he ordered his servants to fill in the grave before daybreak. (8:18).

After this he asked his wife to bake many loaves of bread, and he went out to the herd and brought two steers and four rams and ordered them to be slaughtered. So they began to make preparations. (8:19).

Then he called for Tobias and said to him: “You shall not leave here for fourteen days but shall stay here eating and drinking with me, and you shall cheer up my daughter, who has been depressed. (8:20).

Take at once half of what I own and return in safety to your father; the other half will be yours when my wife and I die. Take courage, my son. I am your father, and Edna is your mother, and we belong to you as well as to your sister now and forever. Take courage, my son.” (8:21).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:18: It is not good that the man should be alone, the words Tobias prays back to God.
Genesis 2:21-24: The woman formed from the man, and the two becoming one flesh.
Leviticus 16:12-13: A censer of coals with incense laid on it so the smoke rises.
Judges 14:12: A wedding celebration lasting seven days.
Revelation 20:1-2: An angel seizes the ancient serpent and binds him.

translationNotes.note: A Hebrew word carried untranslated into Greek and English, meaning firm, sure, reliable. Saying it makes the prayer just spoken the speaker's own, which is why Tobias and Sarah both say it together.

Burial followed death within the day in that climate, so a household expecting a death prepared the grave in advance. Raguel plans to bury and refill before daybreak so that no one outside the house learns of it.

A wedding feast in Israel normally ran seven days (Judges 14:12; Genesis 29:27). Raguel binds himself by oath to a double term, and the guests remain in the bride's father's house for the whole of it.

Only-born, the single child and sole heir of a household. Tobias and Sarah are each an only child, which is why both families fear the line ending. The same word describes the daughter of Jairus in Luke 8:42 and the widow's son at Nain in Luke 7:12.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobias lays the fish's liver and heart on the embers, and the odor drives the demon to the farthest parts of Egypt, where Raphael binds him hand and foot. He and Sarah pray, then sleep. Raguel digs a grave at night; finding the pair alive, he fills it in and holds a fourteen-day feast.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 9
summaryBullets: Then Tobias called Raphael and said to him, (9:1).

“Azariah, my brother, take four servants and two camels with you and travel to Rages. Go to the home of Gabael, give him the bond, get the money, and then bring him with you to the wedding celebration. (9:2).
You are witness to the oath Raguel has sworn, and I cannot violate his oath.” (9:3).
For you know that my father must be counting the days, and if I delay even one day I will upset him very much. (9:4).

So Raphael with the four servants and two camels went to Rages in Media and stayed with Gabael. Raphael gave him the bond and informed him that Tobit’s son Tobias had married and was inviting him to the wedding celebration. So Gabael got up and counted out to him the money bags, with their seals intact, and they put them together. (9:5).

In the morning they both got up early and went to the wedding celebration. When they came into Raguel’s house, they found Tobias reclining at table. He sprang up and greeted Gabael, who wept and blessed him with the words, “Good and noble son of a father good and noble, upright and generous! May the Lord grant the blessing of heaven to you and your wife and to your father and to the mother of your wife. Blessed be God, for I see in Tobias the very image of my cousin Tobit.” (9:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 24:10: A servant sets out on his master's errand with camels and goods in hand.
Jeremiah 32:9-14: A sealed deed of purchase weighed out, witnessed, and stored as legal proof.
2 Kings 12:10: Silver counted out and tied up in bags by the king's secretary and the priest.
Numbers 30:2: A man who swears an oath must not break his word but do all that he said.

translationNotes.note: Silver was weighed rather than counted as coin, then tied into bags and stamped with a clay or wax seal. An unbroken seal was the proof that nobody had opened the bag or shorted the weight since the day of deposit.
A Median city at modern Rey, on the southern edge of Tehran, about 180 miles (290 km) northeast of Ecbatana in mountainous country. Tobit's silver had sat there in trust for twenty years.

The pack animal of long highland and desert routes, able to carry a heavy load for days between waterings. Ten talents of silver weigh roughly 300 kilograms, so the money alone is a pack animal's work to move.
Anepsios means cousin or close kinsman. This book uses several different family words for relatives, so English versions render them as brother, kinsman, or cousin depending on the sentence.

stories.keyTakeaway: Held at Ecbatana by Raguel's oath, Tobias sends Raphael to Rages with four servants and two camels to give Gabael the bond and collect the money. Gabael counts out the bags with their seals intact, and both return for the feast, where he blesses Tobias as the image of Tobit.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 10
summaryBullets: Now day by day Tobit kept counting how many days Tobias would need for going and for returning. And when the days had passed and his son did not appear, (10:1).
he said, “Is it possible that he has been detained? Or that Gabael has died, and there is no one to give him the money?” (10:2).
And he began to worry. (10:3).
His wife Anna said, “My son has perished and is no longer among the living.” And she began to weep and mourn for her son, saying, (10:4).
“Woe to me, my child, the light of my eyes, that I let you make the journey.” (10:5).

But Tobit kept saying to her, “Be quiet and stop worrying, my sister; he is all right. Something must have happened to delay them. The man who went with him is trustworthy and is one of our own kin. Do not grieve for him, my sister; he will be here soon.” (10:6).

She answered him, “Be quiet yourself! Stop trying to deceive me! My son has perished.” She would rush out every day and watch the road her son had taken and would heed no one. When the sun had set she would go in and mourn and weep all night long, getting no sleep. Now when the fourteen days of the wedding celebration had ended that Raguel had sworn to observe for his daughter, Tobias came to him and said, “Send me back, for I know that my father and mother do not believe that they will see me again. So I beg of you, father, to let me go so that I may return to my own father. I have already explained to you how I left him.” (10:7).
But Raguel said to Tobias, “Stay, my son, stay with me; I will send messengers to your father Tobit, and they will inform him about you.” (10:8).
But he said to him, “No! I beg you to send me back to my father.” (10:9).
So Raguel stood and gave Tobias his wife Sarah, as well as half of all his property: male and female slaves, oxen and sheep, donkeys and camels, clothing, money, and household goods. (10:10).

Then he saw them safely off; he embraced Tobias and said to him, “Farewell, my son; have a safe journey. The Lord of heaven prosper you and your wife Sarah, and may I see children of yours before I die.” (10:11).

Then he said to his daughter Sarah, “My daughter, go to your father-in-law and your mother-in-law, since from now on they are as much your parents as those who gave you birth. Go in peace, daughter, and may I hear a good report about you as long as I live.” Then he bade them farewell and let them go. Then Edna said to Tobias, “My child and dear brother, the Lord of heaven bring you back safely, and may I live long enough to see children from you and of my daughter Sarah before I die. In the sight of the Lord I entrust my daughter to you; do nothing to make her unhappy all the days of your life. Go in peace, my son. From now on I am your mother, and Sarah is your sister. May we all prosper together all the days of our lives.” Then she kissed them both and saw them safely off. (10:12).

Tobias parted from Raguel with happiness and joy, praising the Lord of heaven and earth, King over all, because he had made his journey a success, and he blessed Raguel and his wife Edna and said, “May it come to pass that I honor them all the days of their lives.” (10:13).
crossRefs: Genesis 37:34-35: A father mourns a son he believes dead and refuses to be comforted.
Genesis 24:54-56: A traveler insists on being sent back at once though the household asks him to stay.
Genesis 24:59-60: A daughter sent away from her family with a blessing on her and her descendants.
Genesis 31:55: Laban kisses his daughters and grandchildren, blesses them, and returns home.

translationNotes.note: The Assyrian capital on the east bank of the Tigris, opposite modern Mosul in Iraq. It stands roughly 400 miles (600 km) west of Ecbatana, weeks of travel each way by caravan, which is why Tobit can only count days and guess.

Israelite marriage involved both a bride price paid by the groom's side and property sent away with the daughter. Sarah has no brother, so Raguel hands over half his estate at once and pledges the rest at his death.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֶבֶד / שִׁפְחָה (eved / shifchah) - Greek: παῖδες καὶ παιδίσκαι (paides kai paidiskai)
translationNotes.note: Household servants held as property and listed in an estate alongside oxen, sheep, donkeys, camels, and goods. They transfer with the settlement, which is how the inventory in this chapter is meant to be read.

Marriage joined two households, so the in-law relation was spoken of in parent and child terms. Raguel and Edna calling themselves Tobias's father and mother is the ordinary language of that bond, not a legal adoption.

stories.keyTakeaway: In Nineveh Tobit counts the days while Anna mourns her son as lost, watching the road and weeping at night. At Ecbatana, when the fourteen wedding days end, Tobias insists on going home; Raguel gives him Sarah with half of all he owns and sends the couple off with blessings.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 11
summaryBullets: When they came near to Kaserin, which is opposite Nineveh, Raphael said, (11:1).
“You are aware of how we left your father. (11:2).
Let us run ahead of your wife and prepare the house while they are still on the way.” (11:3).
As they went on together, Raphael said to him, “Have the gall ready in your hand.” And the dog went along behind them. (11:4).
Meanwhile Anna sat looking intently down the road by which her son would come. (11:5).
When she caught sight of him coming, she said to his father, “Look, your son is coming, and the man who went with him!” (11:6).
Raphael said to Tobias before he had approached his father, “I know that his eyes will be opened. (11:7).
Smear the gall of the fish on his eyes; the medicine will make the white films shrink and peel off from his eyes, and your father will regain his sight and see the light.” (11:8).
Then Anna ran up to her son and threw her arms around her son, saying, “Now that I have seen you, my son, I am ready to die.” And she wept. (11:9).
Then Tobit got up and came stumbling out through the courtyard door. Tobias went up to him, (11:10).
with the gall of the fish in his hand, and blew it into his eyes, then took hold of him, saying, “Take courage, father.” With this he applied the medicine on his eyes, (11:11).
and it stung. (11:12).
Next, with both his hands he peeled off the white films from the corners of his eyes. Then Tobit threw his arms around him, (11:13).
and he wept and said to him, “I see you, my son, the light of my eyes!” Then he said, “Blessed be God. May his great name be upon us, and blessed be all the angels throughout all the ages. (11:14).

Though he afflicted me, now I see my son Tobias!” So Tobit went in rejoicing and praising God at the top of his voice. Tobias reported to his father that his journey had been successful, that he had brought the money, that he had married Raguel’s daughter Sarah, and that she was, indeed, on her way there, very near to the gate of Nineveh. (11:15).

Then Tobit, rejoicing and praising God, went out to meet his daughter-in-law at the gate of Nineveh. When the people of Nineveh saw him coming, walking along in full vigor and with no one leading him, they were amazed. (11:16).

Before them all, Tobit acknowledged that God had been merciful to him and had restored his sight. When Tobit met Sarah the wife of his son Tobias, he blessed her, saying, “Come in, my daughter, and be welcome. Blessed be your God who has brought you to us, my daughter. Blessed be your father and your mother, blessed be my son Tobias, and blessed be you, my daughter. Come in now to your home, and be welcome, with blessing and joy. Come in, my daughter.” So on that day there was rejoicing among all the Jews who were in Nineveh. (11:17).
Ahikar and his nephew Nadab were also present to share Tobit’s joy. (11:18).
crossRefs: Genesis 46:29-30: A father embraces the son he thought lost and says he is ready now to die.
Luke 15:20: A father sees his son a long way off, runs to him, and throws his arms around him.
Psalm 146:8: The LORD opens the eyes of the blind and lifts up those bowed down.
John 9:6-7: A blind man's eyes are anointed, he washes, and he comes back seeing.

translationNotes.note: The verb for smearing salve directly onto the eye. Ancient eye medicine came as a paste or a pressed cake of powder rubbed on the lid, and the same word is used of eye ointment in Revelation 3:18.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹר עֵינַי (or enai) - Greek: τὸ φῶς τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν μου (to phos ton ophthalmon mou)
translationNotes.note: A Hebrew idiom for what is most precious and life-giving to a person. Anna uses it of her son while Tobit is blind, and Tobit says it back the moment he can see.

The gate was the public square of an ancient city: elders judged there, contracts were witnessed there, and everyone arriving or leaving passed through it. Tobit walking out to the gate with nobody leading him is therefore a public event.
By the Greek period the word covered any member of the covenant people, not only the tribe of Judah. Tobit is of Naphtali, yet the exiles celebrating with him in Nineveh are called Jews.

stories.keyTakeaway: Near Nineveh, Raphael has Tobias go on ahead with the fish gall ready in his hand. Anna sees him and throws her arms around him; Tobit stumbles out, and Tobias blows the gall into his eyes and peels away the white films until his father sees him. Tobit walks unaided to the gate to welcome Sarah.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 12
summaryBullets: When the wedding celebration was ended, Tobit called his son Tobias and said to him, “My son, see to paying the wages of the man who went with you, and give him a bonus as well.” (12:1).
He replied, “Father, how much shall I pay him? It would do me no harm to give him half of the possessions brought back with me. (12:2).
For he has led me back safely, cured my wife, brought the money back with me, and healed you. How much extra shall I give him as a bonus?” (12:3).
Tobit replied, “He deserves, my son, to receive half of all that he brought back.” (12:4).
So Tobias called him and said, “Take for your wages half of all that you brought back, and farewell.” (12:5).

Then Raphael called the two of them privately and said to them, “Bless God and acknowledge him in the presence of all the living for the good things he has done for you. Bless and sing praise to his name. With fitting honor declare to all people the deeds of God. Do not be slow to acknowledge him. (12:6).
It is good to conceal the secret of a king and to acknowledge and reveal the works of God with proper honor. Do good, and evil will not overtake you. (12:7).
Prayer with fidelity is good, and almsgiving with righteousness is better than wealth with injustice. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold, (12:8).
for almsgiving saves from death and purges away every sin. Those who give alms will enjoy a full life, (12:9).
but those who commit sin and do wrong are their own enemies. (12:10).

“I will now declare the whole truth to you and will conceal nothing from you. Already I have declared it to you when I said, ‘It is good to conceal the secret of a king but to reveal with due honor the works of God.’ (12:11).
So now when you and Sarah prayed, it was I who brought the record of your prayers before the glory of the Lord, and likewise whenever you would bury the dead. (12:12).
And that time when you did not hesitate to get up and leave your dinner to go and lay out that corpse, (12:13).
I was sent to you to test you. And at the same time God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law. (12:14).
I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand ready and enter before the glory of the Lord.” (12:15).
The two of them were shaken and threw themselves face down, for they were afraid. (12:16).
But he said to them, “Do not be afraid; peace be with you. Bless God forevermore. (12:17).
As for me, when I was with you, I was not acting on my own will but by the will of God. Bless him each and every day; sing his praises. (12:18).
When you were watching me, I was not really eating anything, but what you saw was a vision. (12:19).
So now bless the Lord on the earth and acknowledge God. See, I am ascending to him who sent me. Write down all these things that have happened to you.” And he ascended. (12:20).
Then they stood up and could see him no more. (12:21).
They kept blessing God and singing his praises, and they acknowledged God for these marvelous deeds of his, that an angel of God had appeared to them. (12:22).
crossRefs: Judges 13:15-21: Manoah offers food to a visitor who proves to be the angel of the LORD and ascends in the flame.
Luke 1:19: I am Gabriel, who stand in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you.
Revelation 8:2: The seven angels who stand before God.
Daniel 8:17: A man falls on his face in terror as a heavenly messenger approaches.
Proverbs 11:4: Riches do not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.

translationNotes.note: Both words mean messenger. The word names the one sent and the sending, and Scripture uses the same term elsewhere of human messengers and of prophets.
The name is built from rapha, to heal, and El, God, so it means God heals. It is formed exactly like Michael and Gabriel, which put other statements about God into a name.

translationNotes.term: Stand before the glory of the Lord
translationNotes.note: Court language. To stand in a king's presence is to be an attendant on duty, waiting to be sent. The phrase describes an assignment and a station, not a posture.
A king's private counsel, which a servant of the court is bound to keep quiet. The saying sets that duty of silence against the works of God, which are to be told out loud in public.

stories.keyTakeaway: Told to pay their companion, Tobias offers half of all they brought back. He takes the two aside, tells them to bless God and declare His works, then tells the whole truth: he carried their prayers before the Lord, and he is Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand before God. Then he ascends.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 13
summaryBullets: Then Tobit said: “Blessed be God who lives forever, and blessed be his kingdom. (13:1).
For he afflicts, and he shows mercy; he leads down to Hades in the lowest regions of the earth, and he brings up from the great abyss, and there is nothing that can escape his hand. (13:2).
Acknowledge him before the nations, O children of Israel, for he has scattered you among them. (13:3).
He has shown you his greatness even there. Exalt him in the presence of every living being, because he is our Lord, and he is our God; he is our Father, and he is God forever. (13:4).
He will afflict you for your iniquities, but he will again show mercy on all of you. He will gather you from all the nations among whom you have been scattered. (13:5).

If you turn to him with all your heart and with all your soul, to do what is true before him, then he will turn to you and will no longer hide his face from you. So now see what he has done for you; acknowledge him at the top of your voice. Bless the Lord of righteousness, and exalt the King of the ages. In the land of my exile I acknowledge him and show his power and majesty to a nation of sinners: ‘Turn back, you sinners, and do what is right before him; perhaps he may look with favor upon you and show you mercy.’ (13:6).
As for me, I exalt my God, and my soul rejoices in the King of heaven. (13:7).
Let all people speak of his majesty and acknowledge him in Jerusalem. (13:8).
O Jerusalem, the holy city, he afflicted you for the deeds of your hands but will again have mercy on the children of the righteous. (13:9).

Acknowledge the Lord worthily, and bless the King of the ages, so that your tent may be rebuilt for you with joy. May he cheer all those within you who are captives and love all those within you who are distressed, to all generations forever. (13:10).

A bright light will shine to all the remotest parts of the earth; many nations will come to you from far away, the inhabitants of the ends of the earth to your holy name, bearing gifts in their hands for the King of heaven. Generation after generation will give joyful praise in you; the name of the chosen city will endure forever. (13:11).

Cursed are all who reject you and all who blaspheme you; cursed are all who hate you and all who speak a harsh word against you; cursed are all who conquer you and pull down your walls, all who overthrow your towers and set your homes on fire. But blessed forever will be all who build you up. (13:12).
Rejoice, then, and exult over the children of the righteous, for they will all be gathered together and will bless the Lord of the ages. (13:13).

Happy will be those who love you, and happy are those who will rejoice in your peace. Happy also all people who grieve with you because of your afflictions, for they will rejoice with you and witness all your joy forever. (13:14).
My soul blesses the Lord, the great King, (13:15).

for Jerusalem will be rebuilt as his house for all ages. How happy I will be if a remnant of my descendants should survive to see your glory and acknowledge the King of heaven. The gates of Jerusalem will be built with sapphire and emerald and all your walls with precious stones. The towers of Jerusalem will be built with gold and their battlements with pure gold. (13:16).
The streets of Jerusalem will be paved with ruby and with stones of Ophir. (13:17).
The gates of Jerusalem will sing hymns of joy, and all her houses will cry, ‘Hallelujah! Blessed be the God of Israel!’— and the blessed will bless the holy name forever and ever.” (13:18).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 30:1-5: Scattered among the nations, then gathered again when they return to the LORD with all their heart.
Isaiah 60:1-11: Light rising over the city, nations coming from far off and bringing their gifts.
Isaiah 54:11-12: Foundations of sapphires, battlements of rubies, and gates of sparkling stones.
Revelation 21:18-21: A city of jasper and gold, with gates of pearl and streets of pure gold.
Psalm 137:5-6: Exiles who refuse to forget Jerusalem.

translationNotes.note: A command addressed to a group: praise Yah. Yah is the short form of the divine name, so the word is left untranslated in Greek and in English rather than rendered as praise the Lord.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם (melekh olam) - Greek: βασιλεὺς τῶν αἰώνων (basileus ton aionon)
translationNotes.note: The Greek aion means an age or span of time, not the world as a place. The title means ruler over all ages, and it appears again in 1 Timothy 1:17.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֹהֶל / מִשְׁכָּן (ohel / mishkan) - Greek: σκηνή (skene)
translationNotes.note: The word for the tabernacle, the tent that housed God's presence in the wilderness. It is used here of the rebuilt city and temple as God's dwelling place, not of a canvas structure.
A distant land, reached by ship in Solomon's day, that supplied Israel's finest gold and gemstones (1 Kings 9:28; 10:11). Stones of Ophir is a way of saying the best obtainable anywhere.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobit sings a hymn: God afflicts and shows mercy, brings down to Hades and raises up, and scattered Israel among the nations. He calls the exiles to turn back with their whole heart, curses those who tear Jerusalem down, blesses those who build it, and sees the city rebuilt in sapphire and gold.

stories.title: 📜 Tobit 14
summaryBullets: So ended Tobit’s words of praise. (14:1).

He died in peace when he was one hundred twelve years old and was buried with great honor in Nineveh. He was fifty-eight years old when he lost his eyesight, and after regaining it he lived in prosperity, giving alms. He continued to bless God and to acknowledge God’s greatness. (14:2).
When he was about to die, he called his son Tobias and his seven children and gave this command: “My son, take your children (14:3).

and escape off to Media, for I believe the word of God that Nahum spoke about Nineveh, that all these things will occur and will happen to Assyria and Nineveh. Indeed, everything that was spoken by the prophets of Israel whom God sent will occur. None of all their words will fail, but all will come true at their appointed times. So it will be safer in Media than among the Assyrians or in Babylon. For I know and believe that whatever God has said will be fulfilled and will occur; not a single word of the prophecies will fail. All of our kindred, inhabitants of the land of Israel, will be counted and taken as captives from the good land, and the whole land of Israel will be desolate; even Samaria and Jerusalem will be desolate. And the temple of God in it will be burned to the ground and will be desolate for a while. (14:4).

“But God will again have mercy on them, and God will bring them back into the land of Israel, and they will rebuild the temple but not like the first one until the appointed time is completed. After this they all will return from their exile and will rebuild Jerusalem in splendor, and in it the temple of God will be rebuilt, just as the prophets of Israel have said concerning it. (14:5).
Then all the nations in the whole world will all be converted and will truly fear God. They will all abandon all their idols who deceitfully have led them into their error, (14:6).

and in righteousness they will praise the eternal God. All the Israelites who are saved in those days and are truly mindful of God will be gathered together; they will go to Jerusalem and live in safety forever in the land of Abraham, and it will be given over to them. Those who sincerely love God will rejoice, but those who commit sin and injustice will vanish from all the earth. (14:7).
So now, my son, leave Nineveh; do not remain here. (14:8).

“So now, my children, I command you, serve God faithfully and do what is pleasing in his sight. Your children are also to be commanded to do what is right and to give alms and to be mindful of God and to bless his name at all times with sincerity and with all their strength. (14:9).

On whatever day you bury your mother beside me, do not stay overnight within the confines of the city, for I see that there is much injustice within it and that much deceit is practiced within it, while the people are without shame. See, my son, what Nadab did to Ahikar, who had reared him. Was he not, while still alive, brought down into the earth? For God repaid him to his face for this shameful treatment. Ahikar came out into the light, but Nadab went into the eternal darkness because he tried to kill Ahikar. Because he gave alms, he escaped the fatal trap that Nadab had set for him, but Nadab fell into it himself and was destroyed. (14:10).

So now, my children, see what almsgiving accomplishes and what injustice does—it brings death! But now my breath fails me.” Then they laid him on his bed, and he died, and he received an honorable funeral. (14:11).
When Tobias’s mother died, he buried her beside his father. Then he and his wife returned to Media and settled in Ecbatana with Raguel his father-in-law. (14:12).
He looked after his parents-in-law with great respect in their old age and buried them in Ecbatana of Media. He inherited both the property of Raguel and that of his father Tobit. (14:13).
He died highly respected at the age of one hundred seventeen years. (14:14).

Before he died he saw and heard of the destruction of Nineveh, and he saw its prisoners being led into Media, those whom King Cyaxares of Media had taken captive. Tobias blessed God for all he had done to the people of Nineveh and Assyria; before he died he rejoiced over Nineveh, and he blessed the Lord God forever and ever. Amen. (14:15).
crossRefs: Nahum 3:1-7: The oracle against the city of blood that Tobit names as certain to happen.
2 Kings 25:8-9: The temple burned and the city left desolate, the disaster Tobit foretells.
Ezra 3:12: The second temple's foundation wept over by those who had seen the first one.
Genesis 49:29-33: A dying father gives his sons his burial instructions and then dies.
Isaiah 2:2-3: Nations streaming to the mountain of the LORD to be taught His ways.

translationNotes.note: Ahikar served as chief of accounts and keeper of the signet under Sennacherib and Esar-haddon, and Tobit names him as his own nephew. An Aramaic papyrus from the fifth century BC, recovered at the Jewish colony of Elephantine in Egypt, preserves his sayings along with the account of the adopted nephew who informed against him and was destroyed in his place.
The prophet whose entire book is an oracle against Nineveh; his name means comfort. Tobit cites him as already spoken and treats the fall of the city as fixed.
The Median king whose army joined Babylon to storm Nineveh in 612 BC, ending the Assyrian empire and carrying its people off as captives. The closing verse places Tobias alive to hear the news.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קֶבֶר אָבוֹת (qever avot) - Greek: τάφος (taphos)
translationNotes.note: Families shared a burial place, often a rock-cut tomb reopened for each death. Asking to have a wife laid beside her husband, and parents-in-law buried where they lived, follows the same custom that Scripture calls being gathered to one's people.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tobit charges Tobias to take his children and escape to Media, since Nahum's word against Nineveh will come true, and recalls how Nadab's plot against Ahikar destroyed Nadab instead. He dies at one hundred twelve; Tobias buries both parents, settles at Ecbatana, and lives to see Nineveh fall.
